item.title: Kenrokuen Garden: One of Japan's Three Great Gardens — Guide
item.description: Kenrokuen Garden is ranked among Japan’s three most celebrated landscape gardens, its name meaning ‘garden of six attributes’, referring to the qualities of spaciousness, seclusion, artifice, antiquity, water and panoramic views that traditional garden theory considered essential to a perfect garden. Developed by the Maeda clan over roughly two centuries, the garden combines ponds, streams, teahouses and trees several hundred years old, and each winter its pine trees are fitted with distinctive rope supports called yukitsuri to protect their branches from heavy snowfall, creating a striking seasonal sight.
